_comment: Third-party skill packages that pair well with a Magpie family, and where to get
them for the harness you actually use.
Magpie recommends none of these as a dependency: every family works with none of
them installed. They are named because a maintainer who has just installed, say,
the security family is about to go looking for exactly this, and the answer
differs per harness in a way no single install line can express.
Rules for an entry, enforced by tools/dev/check-companion-skills.py:
- `harnesses` names every harness the package is actually available on, with
that harness's own install command. A package present on one harness only
says so; the generated block then tells a Codex user it is not for them
rather than printing a command that cannot work.
- `url` points at the package's own documentation, never at a directory site,
so the link survives a directory going away.
- `why` says what it adds *to that family*. An entry that cannot say this is
an advert, not a recommendation, and does not belong here.
- `vendor` is recorded because docs/vendor-neutrality.md is a live metric and
a reader deserves to see whose tool they are being pointed at.

companions.title: Superpowers
companions.what: A skills library and development methodology: brainstorming, plan writing, subagent-driven execution, systematic debugging.

why.utilities: write-skill and optimize-skill author Magpie skills; Superpowers' brainstorming and plan-writing skills are the discipline for deciding what a skill should do before writing it.
why.pairing: self-review and multi-agent-review are pre-flight reads of your own diff; Superpowers adds the test-first and systematic-debugging habits upstream of them.

harnesses.cursor: install from github.com/obra/superpowers through Cursor's plugin flow
harnesses.opencode: clone the skills you want into .opencode/skills/ from github.com/obra/superpowers

companions.note: Ships a plugin manifest per harness and one shared skills/ tree, the same shape Magpie uses, so it is not a Claude Code-only package.

companions.title: Claude Security
companions.what: A multi-agent vulnerability scan of your own repository, run inside the session; each finding carries a severity, a CWE category and reproduction steps, and the ones you pick become patch files you review before applying.

why.security: This family handles reports that arrive — intake, triage, CVE, advisory. Scanning finds the ones nobody reported. The two meet at security-issue-import-from-scan, which imports scanner output as trackers.
why.repo-health: The audits here read dependencies, workflows and licences. This reads the project's own code, which none of them do.

companions.note: Claude Code only: it drives subagents and a scan workflow that Agent Plugins 1.0 has no component for. Listed with its harness named rather than presented as the answer for everyone.

companions.title: Aikido Security
companions.what: SAST, secrets and infrastructure-as-code scanning surfaced in the session.

why.security: A second opinion from a conventional scanner, and a different class of finding — committed secrets — from the ones a code-reading scan surfaces.
why.repo-health: Covers the infrastructure-as-code surface that workflow-security-audit does not read.

companions.title: Code Review
companions.what: Automated pull-request review through several specialised agents, scored by confidence.

why.pr-management: pr-management-code-review walks a maintainer through reviewing one PR at a time and drafts the review they post. This is the other half — a broad automated pass whose findings that review can weigh.
why.pairing: Runs the same kind of pass over a PR that self-review runs over your local diff.
